1305: The Buddha instructed his disciples to go and sit cross-legged under a tree to chant together.
The Buddha instructed his disciples to go and walk slowly under the trees to develop meditation.
The Buddha instructed his disciples to go and sit quietly in a cave to develop meditation.
1306: Sitting meditation helps us have mindfulness, and so sleep far more soundly.
Sitting meditation helps us have patience, and so bear difficulty more easily.
Sitting meditation helps us have mindfulness, and so speak more carefully to others.
1307: Besides sitting meditation, walking meditation also suits those who get sleepy easily.
Besides sitting meditation, walking meditation is what forest monks favour most.
Besides sitting meditation, walking meditation also trains patience just as well.
1308: Insight practice is continually observing the arising and passing of every feeling.
Insight practice is continually observing the changing nature of the body and the mind.
Insight practice is continually returning the attention to the breath itself.
1309: The most popular meditation method is anapanasati — counting each breath in and out.
The most popular meditation method is metta — sending goodwill to all beings.
The most popular meditation object is the breath — chosen because it is always there.
1310: While sitting in meditation, we gradually come to see how restless the mind is.
While sitting in meditation, we gradually stop fighting the thoughts that keep on arising.
While sitting in meditation, we gradually notice sounds we would never normally hear at all.
1311: Even meditating just ten minutes a day, the body can still relax properly.
Even meditating just ten minutes a day, the habit is what matters most.
Even meditating just ten minutes a week, the mind can still grow calmer.
1312: When one attains the first jhana — the first of the form-jhanas — the breath grows very fine.
When one attains the second jhana — the second of the form-jhanas — one feels great rapture and bliss.
When one attains the first jhana — the first of the form-jhanas — thinking itself falls quiet.
1313: Monks often teach having mindfulness and clear comprehension — knowing what one is doing and why.
Monks often teach having patience and contentment — the two hardest things for a householder.
Monks often teach having mindfulness and clear comprehension — even while eating and washing.
1314: Practising the Dhamma helps us see things as they really are, not as others describe them.
Practising the Dhamma helps us bear what cannot be changed, rather than resent it.
Practising the Dhamma helps us see our own faults, before we see anyone else's.
